{{Quote|My critics have often scoffed that I cannot see the galaxy for the systems, for I tend to get bogged down on individual personalities. I believe the smallest pieces are as important as the whole they make, which is why I approach history&mdash;even current history&mdash;from the individuals who help create it.|Voren Na'al|<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook">''[[Dark Force Rising Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
'''Voren Na'al''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Historian/Legends|historian]] in the service of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], and [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]]. He began his career as a [[Journalist/Legends|reporter]] for the [[Galactic News Service]]. His experiences and imprisonment during the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Crackdown on Corsin|overthrow]] of the government of [[Corsin/Legends|Corsin]] drove him into the arms of the Alliance. There, after a stint as a [[Spy/Legends|spy]], he became a historian under [[Master Historian]] [[Arhul Hextrophon/Legends|Arhul Hextrophon]], tasked with compiling the histories of the [[Heroes of Yavin/Legends|Heroes of Yavin]]. Na'al traveled to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and [[Galvoni III]] to acquire information and context on the events preceding the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|battle]] and conducted interviews with the participants, submitting the information in a report to Hextrophon. Subsequent reports included an attempt to discover the truth behind [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca's]] adventures on [[Aduba-3/Legends|Aduba-3]], a 168,000-[[Data screen unit|DSU]] report on the Rebel Alliance for [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], an account of the events surrounding the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] and the tribulations of the Heroes of Yavin afterward, a report on the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], and a piece on the [[Battle of Turak IV]].

With the dawn of the New Republic, Na'al's historical works led him to continued advancement. He became the [[Director/Legends|Director]] of [[New Republic Council Research]] and Assistant Historian to the Republic, and he created reports on [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn's]] and the resurrected [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] campaigns, as well as of Han Solo's experiences in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]] years before. He also compiled the ''[[Oral History of the New Republic]]'', and later edited and annotated "[[Ten Years After: Notes on the Mature Organizational and Administrative Structure of the New Republic]]," an article by the Chief Historian of the [[Kellmer Institute of Galactic History|Kellmer Institute]].

Na'al retired as Head of New Republic Council Research, becoming a history [[Professor/Legends|professor]] and [[Marriage/Legends|marrying]] former deep-cover spy [[Rivoche Tarkin]], with whom he had several children. After the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], he became [[archivist emeritus]] of the [[Historical Council]] of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], in which capacity he supervised the release of [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|the second edition of an important historical chronicle]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|Many years ago, when I first left my homeworld, I was a wide-eyed young man, eager to see what the galaxy had to offer me. I knew little of the galaxy and little of life. After coming face to face with the harsh brutalities of the Empire, I realized that it was my duty to follow my conscience. I joined the Rebel Alliance. In that time, I went from boy to man, and the Alliance went from childhood to adulthood.|Voren Na'al|<ref name="The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook">''[[The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
Voren Na'al was the son of a [[Human/Legends|Human]] family devastated by the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /><ref name="The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook" /> a [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxywide]] conflict waged between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] between [[22 BBY/Legends|22]] and [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> Na'al lost grandparents, aunts, and uncles in that conflict that he never had the opportunity to meet. As a result, he carried some prejudice regarding the idea of [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] into adulthood.<ref name="The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook" /> Even as a boy, he was interested in the causes of galactic events. History and journalism became hobbies of his, nurtured by his [[Journalist/Legends|journalism]] teacher, [[Arhul Hextrophon/Legends|Arhul Hextrophon]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /><ref name="Galaxy Guide 5">''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref>

His hobbies soon blossomed into a fledgling career, as Na'al became a stringer for the [[Galactic News Service]]. On the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Corsin/Legends|Corsin]] in the [[Greater Plooriod Cluster]], Na'al was first exposed to the depredations of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Na'al was fortunate to get an assignment covering the prestigious [[Swoop/Legends|swoop]] races there. While covering the opening matches, a [[Platoon/Legends|platoon]] of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] burst into the press area and placed everyone under arrest. Na'al was kept in a [[Detention area|detention cell]] for three [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]], visited only occasionally by an [[Interrogation droid/Legends|interrogation droid]] that asked no questions. No reasons were ever given for his incarceration, but later, Na'al discovered that the Galactic Empire had [[Crackdown on Corsin|deposed]] the government of the world and replaced it with one dedicated to the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], dispensing with civil rights and placing the entire population under a police state. The imprisonment of the journalists had been a method of keeping them silent.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" />

Na'al, disturbed by this event, realized he had two options: quit reporting and ignore the growing tyranny of the Empire, or go all-out and show the galaxy what the Empire was becoming. Before he had the opportunity to pursue the more reckless path, he had a chance encounter with his old teacher, Arhul Hextrophon.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /> Hextrophon had been with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] since its inception, and convinced Na'al that the young reporter could make a difference in the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] by joining the Rebellion.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5" />

===Historian for the Rebellion and the Battle of Yavin===
{{Quote|It has long been a maxim of my profession that those who ignore history are doomed to repeat it.|Voren Na'al|<ref name="The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook" />}}
[[File:LeiaHanMedal-ANH.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Na'al (far right) bears a Medal of Bravery at the award ceremony.]]
Na'al was initially made a [[Spy/Legends|spy]],<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia">{{CSWECite|II|351|Na'al, Voren}}</ref> but he was soon placed in the [[Historian Corp]], a special Rebel squad under [[Major/Legends|Major]] Hextrophon, the Alliance's [[Master Historian]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /> While still freshly recruited, Na'al made the acquaintance of a Rebel-sympathizing Imperial [[Cadet/Legends|cadet]] named [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]]. When Darklighter discovered that [[Rivoche Tarkin]], the niece of [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]], was quite willing to spy for the Alliance, he put her in contact with Na'al. Rivoche's precarious position as a deep-cover spy meant that Na'al was one of the few Rebels who knew of her existence, and also one of the most vocal advocates for extracting her before the Empire realized her role.<ref name="Cracken's Rebel Operatives">''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]''</ref>

Within a few years of joining the Rebellion, Na'al had earned the rank of [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]].<ref name="Star Wars Insider 133">{{InsiderCite|133|Rogues Gallery|Rogues Gallery: Celebrating a Rebel Victory!}}</ref> In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> he and Hextrophon were at [[Great Temple/Legends|Massassi Outpost]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] following the Alliance's victory over the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. After the battle, they participated in the [[Royal Award Ceremony/Legends|ceremony]] awarding the [[Medal of Bravery/Legends|Medal of Bravery]] to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]].<ref name="Star Wars Insider 133" /> Na'al was responsible for bearing one of the medals, which [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] handed to [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], who awarded it to Skywalker.<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

[[File:Voren_Cantina.png|thumb|right|320px|Na'al encounters an armed patron of Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina.]]
Hextrophon assigned Na'al to write an account of the Battle of Yavin and the events surrounding it, for inclusion into the ''[[Official History of the Rebellion, Volume One]]''. Starting from the Rebel [[Thila Command|base]] at [[Thila/Legends|Thila]], Na'al took a circuitous route via [[Yuga 2]] and the [[Kuari Princess/Legends|''Kuari Princess'']] to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] to begin his research, under the guise of being a reporter for the [[Imperial News Bureau]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /> On Tatooine, he encountered the [[Squib/Legends|Squib]] trader [[Macemillian-winduarté]] and his business partner, the [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] [[Aguilae]], trying to peddle two [[Droid/Legends|droids]], which Na'al succumbed to purchasing. By chance, these droids happened to be [[R5-D4/Legends|R5-D4]] and an [[EG-6 power droid/Legends|EG-6 power droid]], both of which had been present when Jawas had captured and subsequently sold the droids [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] to Skywalker's [[Lars family/Legends|family]]. After thoroughly cleaning the two droids and interviewing them for all relevant information, he gave the power droid to a needy [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmer]], and sold R5-D4 to [[Tour Aryon]]'s assistant administrator, where the droid spied for the Alliance.<ref name="FF">{{FactFile|60|AST 9-12|R5-D4 Astromech Droid}}</ref><ref name="The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook" /> While in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]], he sought out [[Chalmun/Legends|Chalmun's]] [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Spaceport Cantina]], and interviewed several of the patrons therein.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" />

He then traveled to the Imperial bureaucratic hub of [[Galvoni III]], where he [[Slicer/Legends|sliced]] into restricted [[Computer/Legends|computer]] files at the [[Imperial Records Office/Legends|Imperial Records Office]] to acquire an overview of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] and its crew, only narrowly escaping capture. Upon his return to Thila, Na'al conducted interviews with the [[Heroes of Yavin/Legends|Heroes of Yavin]] themselves, including an interview with Luke Skywalker conducted from the [[Gunner/Legends|gunner's]] seat of Skywalker's [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]] during a patrol of the planet. All the information he acquired on his journey was compiled in a report to Hextrophon.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" />

At some point following the Battle of Yavin, individuals on Tatooine were accused of being Na'al and his companions, and subsequently wanted for questioning by the planet's Imperial authorities. [[Imperial Prefect]] [[Eugene Talmont]] was investigating a [[Data-tape/Legends|datatape]] left by Na'al on a prior journey to Tatooine, and hoped to interrogate the suspects so he would not have to spend time decoding the tapes. Encouraged to bribe Imperial government [[Agent/Legends|agent]] [[Beeyon Nace]] for information at Chalmun's Cantina, the suspects learned that the [[Prefect/Legends|Prefect]] placed a 1000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on Na'al. Learning Talmont kept the tapes within the planet's [[Regional Government Offices]], the suspects subsequently broke into the building in order to tamper with them. The tapes were decoded, and Talmont found their apparent contents&mdash;a result of the individuals' tampering&mdash;to be completely worthless, and the suspects were let go in what was considered a case of mistaken identity.<ref name="ARA">{{WEGCite|story=A Rebel Agent|book=Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley}}</ref>

===Aduba-3 Assignment===
{{Quote|I hate to say it, Arhul, but I don't think we'll ever find out what exactly happened on Aduba-3.|Voren Na'al|<ref name="Starhoppers">{{GamerCite|4|The Starhoppers of Aduba-3}}</ref>}}
In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], Na'al was tasked by Hextrophon to ascertain the truth of Han Solo and Chewbacca's adventures on [[Aduba-3/Legends|Aduba-3]]. He began by retracing Solo's steps after his departure from Yavin 4, confirming that he encountered the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Crimson Jack/Legends|Crimson Jack]] and his [[Crimson Jack's crew/Legends|gang]], but afterward, sketchy and contradictory information thwarted his attempts to compile a consistent historical narrative the duo's activities. On Aduba-3, Na'al compiled information on the planet from official planetary records and his own observations. He made contact with the [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]] [[Sacred Way/Legends|Sacred Way]] [[Priest/Legends|priest]] known as [[Pera]], who agreed to an interview after Na'al gave a sizable donation to the Sacred Way, and confirmed that Solo and Chewbacca had been in [[Tun Aduban]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]]. He also located the [[Wroonian/Legends|Wroonian]] [[Azoora]] in [[Locru's Central Saloon]], and briefly interviewed her regarding the [[Cloud-Riders/Legends|local swoop gang]]; however, her boyfriend cut the interview short by threatening Na'al with a non-consensual tracheotomy, forcing the historian to concur with [[Graffiti/Legends|graffiti]] in the saloon [[Refresher/Legends|'fresher]] that "blue lady is trouble."<ref name="Starhoppers" />

Attempts to interview any of the surviving so-called "[[Star-Hoppers of Aduba-3]]" came to naught. As most of Aduba-3's population was transient, even finding an eyewitness to the event was fruitless. Second-hand stories conflicted, and Na'al believed them to be heavily tainted by ''[[Eight for Aduba-3: The Saga of the Starhoppers]]'', a sensationalist [[Tri-Nebula Entertainment]] [[holodocumentary]] of the events.<ref name="Starhoppers" />

On his final day on Aduba-3, Na'al regarded the local farmer and former Starhopper [[Jimm Doshun]] as his only hope of getting to the bottom of things. Unfortunately, a death threat from the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Beilert Valance/Legends|Valance]] made him unwilling to talk, and though Na'al interviewed his wife [[Merri Shen Doshun|Merri]], he found her to be unhelpfully credulous, repeating elements from ''Eight for Aduba-3'' that strained Na'al's belief. As his [[Transport/Legends|transport]] was about to depart, he cut the interview short, leaving him despairing of ever knowing what happened on Aduba-3. He struggled with the report until his deadline had come and gone, ruled out requesting an extension due to budgetary constraints, and ultimately accepted the need to submit his partial reports to the [[BRT supercomputer/Legends|BRT supercomputer]] [[Mistress Mnemos]] and send Hextrophon an apologetic missive.<ref name="Starhoppers" />

===The Battle of Hoth and its aftermath===
{{Quote|In the end, I, like my companions, found myself in a desperate race for the safety of the transport while Imperial soldiers swarmed into the evacuated Echo Base.|Voren Na'al|<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3 2E">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]]</ref>}}
Generally impressed with his work, Hextrophon tasked Na'al with generating an executive summary of a 168,000-[[Data screen unit|DSU]] report on the growth, organization, equipment, activities and objectives of the Alliance for [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]]. Na'al completed the summary in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Na'al was relocated from the base on Thila to [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. General [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]], realizing his job as a historian was largely a passive one, put him to work, first on courier duty delivering messages between ranking personnel while the station's communication equipment was still being adapted to the cold, and later in other noncombatant capacities.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>

[[File:VorenNaal.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Voren Na'al during the Rebellion]]
He was present in the command center when [[Bervin]], a Rebel maintaining watch from one of the base's many perimeter posts, sent in a brief, panicked [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] call. He accompanied Major [[Bren Derlin/Legends|Bren Derlin]] to Bervin's post, only to find the sentry gone, with a [[Blood/Legends|blood]] trail leading through a caved-in wall into the Hoth night. Further attacks on sentries occurred, followed by the actual assault: a pack of [[Wampa/Legends|Wampas]] bursting through the snowy walls of the base, driven into berserk rages by the high-pitched acoustic signaling of the base's [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]]. The beasts outside Echo Base were driven off by the determination and weaponry of the Rebel forces, while the ones that had made it into the base were rounded up with recordings of the droids, stunned to incapacitation, and penned in non-vital areas.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3" />

Na'al was again in the command center when General Solo brought in the remains of the self-destructed [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droid]], and aided Echo Base [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] in reconstructing some of the droids memory circuits. As a noncombatant, Na'al was supposed to evacuate aboard the [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|Rebel transport]] [[Quantum Storm/Legends|''Quantum Storm'']], the first transport off the icy world. Instead, he remained behind, assisting the evacuation efforts of the other transports and gathering holo-recordings of the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] from the trenches, though before long he discarded his [[Holorecorder/Legends|holorecorder]] and [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] for the comfort of a [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]]. In the course of the battle, he broke his ankle in a cave-in, but successfully made it to the [[Thon's Orchard/Legends|''Thon's Orchard'']], one of the final transports to escape. He waited patiently at the [[Haven (rendezvous point)|rendezvous point]] for the Heroes of Yavin, who eventually arrived, allowing him to continue his research and write a detailed account of their travails. For his part in the Battle of Hoth, he was awarded the [[Mantooine Medallion/Legends|Mantooine medal of bravery]], and his recordings helped Rebel tacticians analyze the battle.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3" />

===The Battle of Endor and the Alliance of Free Planets===
{{Quote|By all the gods, Arhul &mdash; ''we've won!'' Now that the deed is done and we are victorious, I can honestly say I never really believed we'd do it.|Voren Na'al|<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5" />}}
In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> Na'al was present with the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance fleet]] mustering at [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]] in preparation for the attack on the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] when the Heroes of Yavin returned from their successful rescue of Han Solo. Na'al regarded this event as one of the most inspiring events as his life.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5" /> Na'al was a participant in the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] and the subsequent celebration held by the Rebels and [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] at [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]], where he became somewhat inebriated on a fermented [[grava berry]] brew, and was coaxed into dancing to the ''[[Starfarer's Return]]'' with several Ewoks.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5 2E">[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi'', Second Edition]]</ref>

The day after the celebration (following the subsidence of his [[Hangover/Legends|hangover]]), Na'al departed for Tatooine. His journey was interrupted when an [[Imperial Customs Frigate]] stopped his [[Starship/Legends|starship]], but his cover identity as a stringer for the Galactic News Service, a role he was quite experienced in, went unchallenged by the officious [[Imperial Office of Customs/Legends|Imperial Customs]] official. In Mos Eisley, Na'al found the city in the midst of a gang war as various factions vied to take control of the [[Jabba's criminal empire/Legends|criminal empire]] of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]], whom the Heroes of Yavin had killed in the rescue of Han Solo.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5" /> While in the city, he brought news of the death of [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] to a small celebration being held in honor of the rescue of [[Diew Rejeff]], a [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] and close associate of Chalmun.<ref name="MEAS">''[[Mos Eisley Adventure Set]]''</ref> Na'al soon left Mos Eisley, hiring a [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|repulsorcraft]] to take him to [[Ben Kenobi's home/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi's hut]], and then on to [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]]. There, he spent three days posing as a [[Drug dealer|spice dealer]], agreeing to supply [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]] with spice, to aid [[Ephant Mon/Legends|Ephant Mon]] in overthrowing Fortuna, to aid [[Ree-Yees/Legends|Ree-Yees]] in killing both Fortuna and Mon, avoiding being [[Poison/Legends|poisoned]], and killing a [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] [[Jabba's Gamorrean guards|guard]] in self defense, all while collecting information on the events surrounding the rescue of Han Solo.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5" />

After returning from Tatooine, Na'al was briefly stationed on Endor, where he interviewed General Solo's [[Endor strike team/Legends|strike team]] and the Ewoks who had participated in the ground battle, retraced their steps through the Endorian forest, and reviewed the efforts of [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket]] and other Ewoks to reclaim the [[Endor shield generator bunker]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5" /> However, his furlough on Endor was short-lived, as Mon Mothma gave him orders to take the first transport to the [[Trans-system data storage library|Imperial data storage facilities]] on [[Halowan]] and gather information on the Imperial command structure at Endor.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5 2E" /> With the assistance of [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] and the disruption of Imperial security procedures caused by the Battle of Endor, Na'al was able to capitalize on his cover as an agent of [[Fakir sector/Legends|Fakir sector's]] Moff [[Lorin]] to get full access to everything he was looking for, despite the security code Intelligence had given him being out of date.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5" /> The Imperial record-keeping system was so well organized, Na'al finished his research in a single day. Upon returning to the fleet, Na'al submitted his report on the Battle of Endor to [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5 2E" />

Na'al had also been assigned to research the events of the [[Battle of Turak IV]], and his information gathering on Halowan had included details regarding the forces of Imperial General [[Maltaz]] at the battle, including the two [[Battalion/Legends|battalions]] of the [[Imperial Hammers Elite Armor Unit/Legends|Hell's Hammers]] that were involved in the attack on [[Turak IV]]. He combined the information he gathered on Halowan with interviews with [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Torv Keist]], a survivor of the [[Hitak Harriers]], the Rebel unit that participated in the battle.<ref name="Battle of Turak IV">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/sourcearchive/news20090512.html|text=The Battle of Turak IV|int=The Battle of Turak IV}}.</ref><ref name="Turak Date">Voren Na'al's infiltration of the [[Halowan]] [[Trans-system data storage library|facility]] while posing as an [[Agent/Legends|agent]] of the [[Fakir sector/Legends|Fakir sector's]] [[Moff/Legends|Moff]], mentioned in ''[[The Battle of Turak IV]]'', occurs after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], according to ''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''; but [[Arhul Hextrophon/Legends|Arhul Hextrophon]] is still listed as part of [[Alliance High Command/Legends|''Alliance'' High Command]] in ''The Battle of Turak IV'', indicating the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] had not yet formed. This places Na'al's report within the first [[Standard month/Legends|month]] after [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']], at the end of which the New Republic was [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|formally established]], according to the ''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]''.</ref>

[[File:VorenNaalAddressesNewRepublicProvisionalCouncil-TaBS.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Voren Na'al addresses the New Republic Provisional Council regarding the Invasion of Bakura.]]
A few weeks after the Battle of Endor, Na'al was tasked with presenting the [[Report to the Provisional Council of the Alliance of Free Planets|report]] to the [[New Republic Provisional Council|Provisional Council]] of the [[Alliance of Free Planets]] regarding the [[Invasion of Bakura]]. Na'al's report concluded by advocating for the suppression of information about the [[Ssi-ruu]]k to the galaxy at large, and for committing a task force to negotiate with the [[Ssi-ruuvi Imperium]] from a position of strength. These recommendations were provocative, leading to a challenge by [[Councillor/Legends|Councilor]] [[Borsk Fey'lya]] that Na'al rebuffed.<ref name="The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook">''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Following the believed death of [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] and the Alliance's confiscation of his starship, [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']], Na'al was in a position to influence what happened to the vessel. [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] attempted to persuade Na'al that the ship should be rented to [[Circus/Legends|carnivals]]. Na'al was nearly convinced by Calrissian's idea, but [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Ackbar]] vetoed the plan.<ref name="Dark Empire Sourcebook">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>

===Historian for the New Republic===
{{Quote|In my twenty years of service to the Rebel Alliance and the New Republic, I have been witness to the most important events in this terrible war with the Galactic Empire. I have lived in an era of social and political upheaval which has shaken the very foundations of the galaxy.|Voren Na'al|<ref name="SWRPG2RE" />}}
When Moff [[Abran Balfour/Legends|Abran Balfour]] was deposed by the [[Laramus Base Irregulars]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] organization, Na'al was dispatched to [[Parmic sector/Legends|Parmic sector]] to examine the Moff's [[Fortress/Legends|stronghold]] and any Imperial records stored there. While sifting through those files, he accidentally triggered a defense mechanism which opened a trapdoor. It dropped him into the midst of Balfour's menagerie, leading the timid historian to loudly scream in a manner humorous to the Irregulars. According to General [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]], this made Na'al "uniquely qualified to discuss [[Sentience/Legends|nonsentient]] life forms," a joke which Na'al did not find very funny.<ref name="SWRPG2RE" />

[[File:QuietDeskJob-SWRPG2ERE.png|thumb|left|180px|Voren Na'al on assignment for the New Republic]]
Prior to the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|Liberation of Coruscant]], Na'al interviewed [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] regarding the life of [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel]] for the historian's ''[[Oral History of the New Republic]]''. This work also contained an interview with General Lando Calrissian regarding his victory over [[Norulac Freebooters|Norulac pirates]] at the [[Battle of Taanab/Legends|Battle of Taanab]].<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

Voren Na'al was eventually promoted to the positions of [[Director/Legends|Director]] of [[New Republic Council Research]] and Assistant Historian to the Republic. He compiled [[An Analysis of Crisis|reports]] on the campaigns of [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] against the New Republic<ref name="The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook" /> as well of those of the cloned Palpatine. He also began growing close to former [[New Republic Intelligence Service]] agent Rivoche Tarkin, who provided him with firsthand accounts of the devastation of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in her new profession as journalist.<ref name="Dark Empire Sourcebook" />

Shortly after the [[Battle of Calamari|Battle of Mon Calamari]], Na'al interviewed Han Solo on [[New Ralltiir]] regarding his exploits in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]], hoping to gather information useful to New Republic forces expanding into that region.<ref name="Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook">''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]''</ref> He prepared for this interview by compiling a report on Solo's [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] career from records captured by New Republic Intelligence at the [[Ompersan]] data vault; he later sent this information to Hextrophon.<ref name="TEGW" /> At some point following the final defeat of Palpatine, Na'al interviewed retired [[Governor/Legends|Governor-General]] [[Nahdonnis Praji]] of [[Kaikielius/Legends|Kaikielius]], during which Praji recounted his only encounter with the reborn Emperor.<ref name="Praji">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/praji/20090205.html|text=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji|int=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji}}</ref>

[[File:BizCasFri-SWRPG2ERE.png|thumb|right|140px|Voren Na'al, New Republic historian]]
In [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]], [[Academician]]<ref name="Cracken's Threat Dossier">''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]''</ref><ref name="Academician note">On Earth, an "academician" can be either a term for an academic or intellectual, or a member of an academy. Context is unclear whether Na'al held the title merely as an honorific, or gained it by full membership in an institution. See:<br />{{WebCite|url=https://www.lexico.com/en/definition/academician|text=Academician &#124; Definition of Academician by Oxford Dictionary on Lexico.com also meaning of Academician|author=Oxford University Press|archivedate=20200819083137}}</ref> Na'al, in cooperation with New Republic Intelligence, edited and annotated "[[Ten Years After: Notes on the Mature Organizational and Administrative Structure of the New Republic]]," an article by [[Donn Gulek]], Chief Historian of the [[Kellmer Institute of Galactic History|Kellmer Institute]]. This article, which detailed the structure of the New Republic after its most recent internal reorganization, was included in a New Republic Intelligence dossier on the [[Black Fleet Crisis]].<ref name="Cracken's Threat Dossier" />

===Later years===
{{Quote|I'm a little too old to be hopping around the Outer Rim like an overzealous kid.|Voren Na'al|<ref name="The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook" />}}
Na'al eventually retired as Head of New Republic Council Research, becoming a history [[Professor/Legends|professor]]. He and Rivoche Tarkin were married, and had several children together.<ref name="The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook" /> Their son [[Gideon Na'al|Gideon]], named after [[Gideon Tarkin|Rivoche's father]], later co-authored ''[[Star Maps and Scripts: The Rakata Connection]]'' with [[Doctor/Legends|Dr.]] [[Henrietya Antilles|Corellia Antilles]].<ref name="The Written Word" /><ref name="Blog">{{Blog|JSarek|8|Endnotes for The Written Word}}</ref> Nearly ten years after the destruction of [[Mount Tantiss/Legends|Mount Tantiss]], he enlisted the help of one of his students, the [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] [[Pollo Tipn]], in investigating for Mon Mothma some unusual reports emanating from the [[Kathol sector/Legends|Kathol sector]], reports connected to Grand Admiral Thrawn.<ref name="Field Work">{{WEGCite|story=Field Work|book=The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook}}</ref>

Following the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Na'al became the [[archivist emeritus]] of the Historical Council of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]]. He oversaw the release of [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|the second edition]] of an [[The Essential Chronology|important historical chronicle]], around the time of the events of the [[Killik/Legends|Killik]] [[Dark Nest Crisis|conflict]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> This record included a comprehensive discussion of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] conflict. For [[Tionne Solusar]]'s [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]] [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force|guide]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], Na'al provided information on a Jedi who arrived on [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] in [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]], identifying him as [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] and indicating he stopped a [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] named [[Zalem/Legends|Zalem]] from using the ancient [[Infinity Gate]] to devastate Coruscant. However, Na'al acknowledged that this information was drawn from a single unreliable source, the [[28 BBY/Legends|28 BBY]] memoir of [[Ros Lai]], an alleged former Nightsister.<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I found myself surrounded by a bewildering array of animals&mdash;hissing, purring, growling, thrashing, flying&mdash;that seemed to cover every evolutionary possibility. According to the report filed by the Laramus Regulars, they could 'hear Na'al's screams in vacuum.'<br />"According to General Cracken, this made me 'uniquely qualified to discuss nonsentient lifeforms.'<br />"I will never understand military humor.|Voren Na'al, recalling his mission to [[Spice Terminus/Legends|Spice Terminus]]|<ref name="SWRPG2RE" />}}
Voren Na'al was an unimposing youth when he first volunteered for the Alliance, though his years recording the exploits of the heroes of the galaxy, and his adventures in documenting them, had made him a wiser and more experienced man late in life.<ref name="The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook" /> During both phases of his life, however, he held great enthusiasm for the personalities he reported on;<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /><ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" /> this occasionally led to a nearly unprofessional zeal in his writings, a trait which he was self-conscious of and for which he sometimes felt the need to apologize.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /> His critics also found his writing to be overly focused on individual personalities.<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" /> Nonetheless, his work was quoted by author Dr. [[Milanda Vorgan]] in her seminal work ''[[The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic]]''.<ref name="The Written Word" /> He held his reporting to a high standard, never submitting any work to Hextrophon past deadline, or of which he could not be proud, until the frustrating assignment at Aduba-3 left him little recourse but to upload incomplete reports to Mistress Mnemos, with apologies to Hextrophon.<ref name="Starhoppers" />

[[File:VorenNaalSignature-HanSoloAndTheCorporateSectorSourcebook.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Voren Na'al's signature]]
Later in life, Na'al settled into his role as a family man, and turned down offers to explore abroad; it took a personal and persuasive request by Mon Mothma to convince him to go to the Kathol sector. His advancing age, and concern for the request of his wife that he not go alone, convinced him to take Pollo Tipn along as help.<ref name="The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook" />

Na'al stood 1.8 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /> He was fair complected, with [[Color/Legends|blond]] hair and brown eyes.<ref name="SWRPG2RE" />

==Skills and abilities==
{{Quote|That's very interesting, but what does it really mean?|Voren Na'al|<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3" />}}
Voren Na'al was a historian whose skills helped preserve a record of the Galactic Civil War, contributions that were memorable and valued by the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1 2E">[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope'', Second Edition]]</ref> In particular, his straightforward style of reporting earned him respect and recognition amongst his peers.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5 2E" /> He was generally regarded as neither imposing nor remarkable, but he was intelligent, knowledgeable, dexterous, dedicated despite a slight cowardly streak, and quite lucky. He was adept with computers, having successfully sliced into the restricted computer files of the Imperial Records Office on Galvoni III<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /> and aided Rebel technicians in reconstructing valuable information from the remains of the [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droid]] Han Solo brought back to Echo Base.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3" /> While Na'al was not regarded as skilled at intrigue,<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1 2E" /> he nonetheless was briefly assigned by the Alliance as a spy,<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia" /> and later was able, with the assistance of Alliance Intelligence, to infiltrate the Imperial data storage facility on Halowan in the chaos following the Battle of Endor.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5" /> He had little combat experience, but he survived a [[Lightfight|firefight]] or two prior to the Battle of Hoth.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|I arrived with a holorecorder in one hand and a datapad in the other. But before long I found myself shamelessly abandoning those seemingly useless tools for the cold comfort of a blaster rifle.|Voren Na'al|<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3" />}}
Throughout his research missions during the Galactic Civil War, Voren Na'al carried with him a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]], datapad, [[Holocamera/Legends|holocam]], falsified [[Identichip/Legends|identification]], and 700 credits.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1 2E" /><ref name="Galaxy Guide 3 2E" /><ref name="Galaxy Guide 5 2E" /> At the Battle of Hoth, however, the grim reality of the Imperial advance led Na'al, who was an observer in the trenches outside Echo Base, to set aside his holorecorder and datapad and pick up a blaster rifle.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3" /> In addition, Na'al kept a [[Voren Na'al's journal|personal journal]], wherein he kept private notes about the subjects whom he interviewed in the course of his research.<ref name="LCSB">''[[The Last Command Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Voren Na'al-- the EU chroniclist's ''[sic]'' dream in that he allows a source file author the freedom to blame mistakes on shoddy journalism&hellip;|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|<ref name="Pablog 59">{{Blog|pablog|59|Tales of the Big Green Bunny: Behind the Scenes of Gamer #4 &mdash; Voren Na'al}}</ref>}}
Voren Na'al originated as the [[in-universe]] "author" of several ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' sourcebooks published by [[West End Games]] (WEG), beginning with ''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]'' in [[1989]]. He was created by author and designer [[Grant S. Boucher]]<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /> to provide an in-universe perspective on the subjects WEG covered in its works, and to leave room for uncertainty in these accounts, providing a gamemaster with a handy justification to ignore some facts in a sourcebook for his own campaign.<ref name="Pablog 59" /> The character's name is an [[Tuckerization|anagram]] of the characters Aedon, Oren, and Ty Vaal from one of the author's unpublished manuscripts, while the illustrations of the character (young) are directly based on photos of the author that were provided to WEG.<ref name="Boucher's email">{{EmailCite|email=File:GrantBoucherEmail.png|creator=[[Grant S. Boucher]]|date=2020-01-05}}, regarding [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Voren_Na%27al/Legends?diff=8743623&oldid=8688732 this edit]</ref>

After WEG's bankruptcy, Na'al saw relatively little use.<ref name="Geekosity">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2005/10/new-essential-chronology-talkback.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=The New Essential Chronology: Talkback thread|quote=Voren hasn't been seen much since WEG's implosion in 1995 [sic], but as a fictional character, he seemed like the kind of guy who would get involved in a project like this. As "archivist emeritus," he's apparently moved up in the world.}}</ref> [[Pablo Hidalgo]]'s [[2001]] article "[[The Starhoppers of Aduba-3]]," from [[Star Wars Gamer 4|''Star Wars Gamer'' 4]], used Na'al to introduce uncertainty to its retelling of the [[Marvel Comics]] storyline begun in "[[Star Wars (1977) 8|''Star Wars'' (1977) 8]];" by having Na'al express disbelief at the accounts he was hearing, it also implied that the outlandish camp of the original story was the actual truth.<ref name="Pablog 59" /> He re-appeared as author of the introduction to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' in [[2005]]; author [[Daniel Wallace]] noted that "he seemed like the kind of guy who would get involved in a project like this."<ref name="Geekosity" />

[[File:Rogues_Gallery.jpg|thumb|right|250px|''Star Wars Insider 133'' retroactively established Na'al's presence in the final scene of ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''.]]
In [[2012]], the "[[Rogues Gallery (department)|Rogues Gallery]]" feature in [[Star Wars Insider 133|''Star Wars Insider'' 133]] identified the two extras who bear the medals to General Dodonna as Na'al and Hextrophon, [[Retroactive continuity|retroactively]] establishing that film as their first appearance.<ref name="Star Wars Insider 133" /> The actor playing Na'al was [[Derek Lyons]], who also portrayed one of the [[Rebel Honor Guard/Legends|Rebel Honor Guard]] members depicted earlier in the same scene.<ref name="Lyons 1">{{WebCite|url=http://www.dereklyonssite.com/voren-naal-aka-the-medal-bearer.html|text=VOREN NA'AL AKA THE MEDAL BEARER|author=Lyons, Derek|work=[http://www.dereklyonssite.com DEREK LYONS OFFICIAL SITE]|archivedate=20190317194842}}</ref> The film was the eighteen-year old actor's first. Lyons was chosen for both roles by the assistant director,<ref name="Lyons 2">{{WebCite|url=http://www.dereklyonssite.com/the-bothan-spy-interview.html|text=THE BOTHAN SPY INTERVIEW|author=Lyons, Derek|work=[http://www.dereklyonssite.com DEREK LYONS OFFICIAL SITE]|archivedate=20190411160022}}</ref> [[Terry Madden]],<ref name="Lyons 3">{{WebCite|url=http://www.dereklyonssite.com/the-medal-bearers-story.html|text=THE MEDAL BEARER'S STORY|author=Lyons, Derek|work=[http://www.dereklyonssite.com DEREK LYONS OFFICIAL SITE]|archivedate=20190317194947}}</ref> when he arrived at the studio for a fitting. His scenes were filmed at [[Shepperton Studios]], rather than the main filming location at [[Elstree Studios]] in Borehamwood, due to the need for a large sound stage to represent the immense [[Grand Audience Chamber]] where the medal ceremony takes place. Lyons worked for two weeks on the movie, filming his scene as medal-bearer first, which took over a week as a result of the special effects logistics needed to make approximately one hundred actors portraying Rebels appear to be nearly a thousand (in contrast, filming as the guard took only a few days). While Lyons enjoyed both parts, he was more fond of his time as the medal bearer, as it included him in the film's final scene with the main characters.<ref name="Lyons 2" />

Lyons also appeared in Jan Dodonna's audience of Rebels during the [[Death Star plans/Legends|Death Star plans]] briefing, and again in scenes set in the [[Strategy Center|War Room]] during the battle itself. It is unclear whether he is portraying Na'al, the unnamed Rebel Honor Guard, or another character in these scenes,<ref name="Lyons 4">{{WebCite|url=http://www.dereklyonssite.com/star-wars.html|text=STAR WARS|author=Lyons, Derek|work=[http://www.dereklyonssite.com DEREK LYONS OFFICIAL SITE]|archivedate=20190411151949}}</ref> though Na'al expressly notes in ''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'' that he was not present for the events at the Battle of Yavin.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3" />

The first edition of ''Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope'' ends with Na'al formulating the beginning to a story he would tell based on his research. This beginning is the [[opening crawl]] for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /><ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope" /> The opening crawl is excised from the end of [[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope'', Second Edition]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1 2E" /> In [[1996]], Na'al broke the fourth wall more directly, dispensing [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] advice about the galaxy, gamemaster characters, aliens, creatures, and planets directly to the players in ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''.<ref name="SWRPG2RE" />
